services.desc: General Carl A Spaatz was born in Boyertown in 1891. He was the son of Charles Spaatz, the editor and publisher of the Boyertown Democrat, the newspaper that would become the Boyertown Times. Carl attended West Point Military Academy. General Spaatz would go on to earn the Distinguished Flying Cross for shooting down 2 German planes in France in WWI. In 1929, with Capt. Ira Eaker and Lt. Elwood Quesada, he established an endurance record by staying in flight for more than 159 hours in a Fokker plane named “Question Mark”, proving the viability of midair refueling that enabled long distance flights.
